headline: BNP leader dies of snakebite in Patuakhali; family alleges antivenom was withheld
summary: The family of the deceased BNP leader claims that essential antivenom was not administered at the Upazila Health Complex, leading to his death. This incident has sparked questions regarding medical service availability.
details: A BNP leader in Patuakhali has died following a snakebite, with his family alleging that crucial antivenom was withheld at the local Upazila Health Complex.
The incident occurred in Patuakhali, where the leader was bitten by a snake. He was subsequently taken to the Upazila Health Complex for urgent medical treatment.

Family members claim that the necessary antivenom was not administered, leading to his death. This has sparked concerns regarding the availability of essential medical supplies in rural health facilities.

topic: Pirgachha police station besieged JCD leader death
headline_marked: [[Pirgachha Police Station besieged]] by 200+ protesters over JCD leader's death in Savar
headline: Pirgachha Police Station besieged by 200+ protesters over JCD leader's death in Savar
summary: Relatives and locals surrounded the police station in Rangpur, demanding a fair investigation and punishment for those allegedly involved in the death of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi.
details: Over 200 relatives and local residents besieged Pirgachha Police Station in Rangpur on Saturday, protesting the death of Chhatra Dal leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi. Protesters brought Monowarul’s body to the station premises and blocked the road, alleging police involvement in his death.

Monowarul Hossain Bakshi, 29, vice-president of the Savar unit of JCD, died early Friday after falling from a residential building rooftop. This occurred during a police operation at the Staff Quarters of the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC) in Savar, Dhaka.

Monowarul, son of a BPATC security guard, lived with his father at the residential building. Officers from Pirgachha Police Station, assisted by Savar police, had raided Jafar’s flat while searching for a missing teenage girl and her companion.
The protest escalated after an ambulance carrying Monowarul’s body arrived at the station. Local political leaders intervened, eventually bringing the situation under control.

Mofasirul Islam, member secretary of Pirgachha upazila JCD, demanded a fair investigation to determine the cause of death and identify those involved. He stressed that perpetrators must face justice without harassing innocent individuals.

Aminul Islam Ranga, president of Pirgachha upazila BNP, stated that the circumstances of Monowarul's fall and any police involvement would be clarified by the autopsy, investigation committee report, and legal inquiry.

Mamdel Hossain Bokshi, the deceased's brother, alleged that the missing girl's father went to Savar with police, including one in uniform. He confirmed they are preparing to file a case with Savar Model Police Station, seeking an impartial investigation and punishment for those responsible.

Selim Malik, officer-in-charge of Pirgachha Police Station, confirmed that relatives were advised to file a case. He added that the actual circumstances of the incident would emerge through a thorough investigation.
